sources.label: Illinois Comptroller local government financial database, FY 2023 (Annual Financial Reports)

notes: Actual results for the fiscal year ended November 30, 2023, as the county reported them in its Annual Financial Report to the Illinois Comptroller. Not a budget.
The FY 2024 report was out of balance (revenue and spending more than four times apart) or not yet filed, so FY 2023 is used.

Public schools are run by separate school districts with their own taxes, so they are not included. The county collector gathers property taxes for every taxing district and pays them over; that money is left out.

Covers the general, special revenue, capital projects, debt service and enterprise (utility) funds. Pension trusts and other fiduciary funds, internal service funds and component units are left out, as are transfers between funds and borrowing.
Capital outlay outside utility funds ($3,664,631) is reported without a function, so it is spread over the county's services in proportion to their spending.
Courts, legal services, public buildings, housing and community development count as overhead.
Debt is bonds, contracts and other long-term debt outstanding at year end (beginning balance plus new debt less debt retired), as reported.
Political money is not scored: no county board and county office candidates of Iroquois County reported contributions to the State Board of Elections since 2023.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.

sources.label: Illinois Comptroller local government financial database, FY 2024 (Annual Financial Reports)

notes: Actual results for the fiscal year ended March 31, 2024, as the township reported them in its Annual Financial Report to the Illinois Comptroller. Not a budget.

Public schools are run by separate school districts with their own taxes, so they are not included. Residents also pay Iroquois County; park, library and fire protection districts are separate governments too.
Illinois townships maintain township roads, assess property and provide general assistance; most also cover the cities and villages inside them.

Covers the general, special revenue, capital projects, debt service and enterprise (utility) funds. Pension trusts and other fiduciary funds, internal service funds and component units are left out, as are transfers between funds and borrowing.
Courts, legal services, public buildings, housing and community development count as overhead.
Debt is bonds, contracts and other long-term debt outstanding at year end (beginning balance plus new debt less debt retired), as reported.

Political money is not scored: no candidates for mayor or village president, council or board, clerk and other local offices of Milford Township reported contributions to the State Board of Elections since 2023.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.
